parsed.why: No trans-specific offence; equal-treatment act actually used (airport screening complaint), hate-crime infrastructure, self-ID climate. Negatives are operator-set sauna rules and birth-sex custody placement—real but contingent, mediated by functioning law that works for trans people.

State-imposed universal exposure: sex-at-birth passport/visa rules, screening flags, possible fraud ineligibility; facility bans in ~half the states with trespass arrests; birth-sex custody with abusive practices; threat-framing rhetoric. Courts and some states push back only partially.

No recognition plus state-tolerated targeting: police refusal in LGBT death investigations, gang extortion, mass-raid detention of trans women with shaved hair and punishment drills, no gender accommodation, and 2013 polling showing 85% would accept attacks.

Decriminalisation constitutionally confirmed and entry bans clarified as unenforceable regionally; no documented trans-specific targeting or violence. But the immigration clause remains, trans-specific recourse is thin, and acceptance data are dated and only moderate.

Statutory protections name gender identity and an equality body exists, but enforcement is weak, acceptance is very low (79% reject neighbours), and a 2025-documented trans detainee was isolated by birth sex with humiliating treatment; breakaway region harsher.
